result.reason: Nothing I found kills the idea. No commercial tool for checking gold sellers or keeping a purchase register turned up. QORI, the mandatory Minem app for logging each gold trade (DU 006-2025), is limited to a Pataz pilot, and I found no sign it has gone national. The RECPO regulation is still a 2021 draft, and no 2026 national traceability decree came up. The duty has teeth: in RN 510-2024 the Supreme Court held that buyers must verify where the gold comes from, and signed seller declarations were not enough. Weaknesses: the free SUNAT/INGEMMET lookups already cover single checks. The REINFO cut-off is uncertain (a Congress extension is pending and the Constitutional Court hears the registry's constitutionality on 5 Nov). Many buyers are informal, and the state could still roll QORI out nationally.

result.reason: I found no killer. No local or international SPLAFT software for Peruvian gaming came up, and the state tools (ROSEL, SISDEL, SUCTR) are only filing or machine-monitoring channels. Three things keep the score low. First, the duty isn't new: Res. SBS 01015-2026 replaces Res. 1695-2016, so slot-room operators already have compliance officers and SPLAFT manuals, and many likely use outside consultants such as PRCP. Second, the market is small: an undated MINCETUR presentation to Congress, apparently from 2023, counts about 325 licensed firms running 711 rooms. Online operators are new to the regime but probably use international KYC tools. Third, enforcement is light: 10 firms were fined in 2022 for missing the annual compliance-officer report. Still not checked: the adaptation deadline, any small-firm regime, and RO thresholds. Two key sources returned 403.

result.killer: Not a product: per a municipal ordinance in El Peruano, DS 004-2026-MTC (20 Jan 2026) postponed the entry into force of DS 011-2025-MTC (the Ley 31917 regulation) to 31 Dec 2026. result.reason: I found no association-side software. result.reason: No single kill: I found no compliance-specific product, but the case is weaker than claimed. The UGEL evidence workflow already runs on MINEDU's free platforms. Schools self-report basic conditions in SIMON (PM-49 in 2022, PM-138 in 2024), and UGEL01 collected the art. 44.1 report in its SIIC 01 system. Indecopi and MINEDU also publish guides for parents. Under Ley 32562 the regulation is still only a draft (RM 307-2026-MINEDU). Searches did not confirm a final supreme decree as of Oct 2026, so new duties and deadlines are unsettled. The 30-day cost notice is one letter a year, which SieWeb-type systems and templates can handle. Law firms such as PRC send client memos on the rules. Many targets are tiny or informal.

coverage.found: Markets (mercados de abastos, galerías) need a corporate licencia de funcionamiento (Ley 28976 art. 9) held by the market's collective body; individual stalls get an ITSE ex post, and the ITSE renews every 2 years. Licence validity is indefinite (Surquillo 2026 resolutions confirm). Food handlers need a carné de sanidad from the municipality (6 months if handling food directly, 1 year otherwise, per Andina; varies by ordinance). Meat and fish stalls are inspected by municipalities, not SENASA or SANIPES (these cover slaughterhouses and fishing infrastructure). No 2026 rule change found. Candidate C4 (weak). Not confirmed: whether the market stall carné cycle is digitised by any municipality.

coverage.category: 32. Defensa Civil ITSE / inspección técnica de seguridad en edificaciones for small premises (DS 002-2018-PCM)
coverage.found: DS 002-2018-PCM is still in force: 2026 municipal resolutions still cite it. ITSE certificates last 2 years, and renewal for low and medium risk premises is a tasa plus a declaración jurada (art. 24). High and very high risk premises need a full inspection. No 2026 reform found. The 2020 DL 1497 validity extension is a pandemic item and is no longer relevant. Candidate C5 (weak). Competitors not checked.

coverage.category: 33. Electronic invoicing and SUNAT regime obligations for micro-firms (RUS/RER/RMT), GRE guía de remisión electrónica
coverage.found: RS 000108-2026/SUNAT (29 May 2026, in force 1 Jun) changes who must issue the GRE-remitente. It is aimed at foreign-trade and port transfers. RS 000124-2026/SUNAT moves to 1 Nov 2026 the end of the 'ticket de salida' as a supporting document, which stays valid until 31 Oct 2026. RS 000031-2026 extends SUNAT's non-sanction discretion for paper guides. Scope is narrow (foreign merchandise leaving ports), and issuing is free through SEE-SOL or the SEE del contribuyente. A secondary source says the new RUS is exempt, but this is unverified. Related to K11. Candidate C6 (weak).

coverage.category: 34. Solid-waste and recycling informal collectors (recicladores), Ley 29419 / DS 005-2010-MINAM / DS 001-2022-MINAM
coverage.found: Municipalities keep a Registro Municipal de Organizaciones de Recicladores. Associations need a constancia de formalización (DS 001-2022-MINAM). The register requires the ficha registral, a member list with DNI and waste type, and a sworn statement per member. Sales documents (boletas, facturas, liquidaciones de compra to registered recicladores) support the municipal RSIV indicator in the MEF incentive programme. Santa María del Mar approved a formalization ordinance in Aug 2026. SIGERSOL reporting falls mainly on municipalities. Not found: any 2026 deadline for RSIV reporting, or any software for recycler associations. Candidate C2 (weak, related K03).

coverage.category: 35. Private schools, academies, CETPRO and nurseries (MINEDU / UGEL registration and annual reporting)
coverage.found: Ley 32562 (promulgated 22 Mar 2026 after legislative insistence) modifies Ley 26549. It requires prior authorization from MINEDU, basic conditions (infrastructure, staff, pedagogy, management) and wider information duties to parents. It sets leve/grave/muy grave sanctions, fines up to 100 UIT, closure, and joint liability of the owner or promoter. It repeals DS 005-2021-MINEDU. RM 307-2026-MINEDU (22 May 2026) published the draft regulation for comment, and the final regulation is unconfirmed. The existing duty under art. 14 requires pension and enrolment information in writing at least 30 days before enrolment, and UGELs send oficios demanding evidence (e.g. by 1 Mar 2025). SIAGIE is the free mandatory MINEDU system. A vendor named SieWeb sells school intranet and pension payment. Candidate C1 (promising). Nurseries, CETPRO and academies were not separately searched.

coverage.category: 36. Transport and mototaxi / taxi formalization and operator registers at municipalities (ATU, SUTRAN, municipal permits); SOAT/AFOCAT/CITV
coverage.found: Ley 31917 and its regulation DS 011-2025-MTC (El Peruano, 26 Jul 2025) require mototaxi (L5) service to be provided by a legal entity registered in Registros Públicos and active in RUC. The entity needs a Permiso de Operación and Certificado de Operación from the district municipality, with renewal filed 60 days before expiry (automatic approval). Vehicles need CITV, SOAT or CAT, an authorized colour and the placa. Vests with plate and holographic stickers issued by municipalities were due from 22 Jan 2026. Medical and psychological tests stay mandatory until 31 Dec 2026. DS 004-2026-MTC (20 Jan 2026) sets implementation measures, but the text could not be read (the congreso.gob.pe PDF returned 404). SINARETT will gain a Registro Nacional de Transportadores de Mototaxi. A Congress committee approved an amending bill on 2 Mar 2026. Correo reports that municipalities lack money and staff to apply the rules. DS 005-2024-MTC and DS 004-2024-MTC let CITV and police check SOAT and CAT electronically in the MTC database, so vehicle insurance paperwork is becoming digital. AFOCAT issue the CAT electronico via an MTC web service (Directiva 002-2024-MTC/18). ATU and SUTRAN were not searched. Candidates C7 (promising) and C8 (unverified).

result.competitor: No commercial software was found in two Spanish-language searches for gold traceability / buyer due-diligence tools. The real threat comes from the state. (1) DU 006-2025 (May 2025) requires gold buyers in Pataz to register in RECPO and to record every operation in a mandatory Minem app, QORI, under a 90-day pilot. A separate search found no further details on QORI. (2) 'RECPO En Línea' is a planned platform for due diligence and transaction traceability, to be piloted in Madre de Dios, Arequipa and Puno. (3) In 2023 Minem/DGFM piloted a tech tool for gold purchase and sale operations in Madre de Dios. (4) The 2021 RECPO draft would require buyers to report transactions through a state system. Supplier checks can already be done for free on SUNAT's REINFO lookup and INGEMMET's concession lookup. If QORI or RECPO En Línea is rolled out nationally, it will cover the core register job. A private tool would then be limited to batch checking of supplier status, document storage and audit packs.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. DL 1107 art. 11 was amended by Ley 31746 (El Peruano, 18 May 2023) and, according to a secondary summary, amended again by Ley 32537 (late 2025). It requires anyone who buys controlled mining products to verify their origin on every purchase. Minimum checks: the seller's RUC, name, ID and address; the Código Único de Concesión and whether it is valid; the Autorización de Explotación; current REINFO or similar status; payment vouchers (weight, description); and the guía de remisión and carrier. The buyer must also confirm the data in the official systems. Penalties: illegal purchases give no tax rights or benefits, and Minem and SUNAT can impose administrative sanctions (cms.law). Separately, DS 012-2012-EM art. 5, as amended by DS 034-2017-EM, requires plantas de beneficio and comercializadores to keep an up-to-date electronic register of every gold purchase (seller's RUC and name, current REINFO) and make it available to the inspecting authority. No repeal was found, but I could not confirm the current consolidated text. The REINFO period runs until 31 Dec 2026 or until the Ley MAPE takes effect. The Ley MAPE was still a bill as of July 2026, and the Executive plans a new simplified process for the roughly 31,600 people still in REINFO during 2027. That means suppliers will have to be re-checked around the year-end. The RECPO regulation (2021 draft, RM 190-2021-MINEM-DM, which proposed that buyers report their gold transactions) has not been found as issued.
result.market: RECPO had 12,418 registrants in Feb 2025 (8,790 in June 2021). An ex-Minem official thinks only about 2,000 are genuine. Roughly 6,000 processing plants were cited in Oct 2025, though the claim says 2,328 plantas remain in REINFO after the clean-up. The realistic paying market is likely a few hundred to about 2,000 active, semi-formal buyers and plantas, concentrated in Madre de Dios, Puno, Arequipa, La Libertad and Lima.
result.reason: The duty is real: there is a per-purchase verification duty (DL 1107 art. 11) and an electronic purchase register (DS 012-2012-EM as amended in 2017), and the REINFO cut-off and transition will force buyers to re-check suppliers. I found no commercial product. However, Minem is building its own traceability systems: QORI is already mandatory in Pataz, and RECPO En Línea is being piloted. A national rollout would take over the register job. The checks can be done for free on SUNAT and INGEMMET. Many buyers are informal or launder gold, so they have little reason to want strong verification. Willingness to pay is uncertain, and distribution in remote mining regions is hard. The legal framework keeps shifting (Ley MAPE is pending), which makes it risky for a solo founder. A niche exists for semi-formal buyers that need export or refinery KYC, but it is narrow.

result.competitor: I found no commercial SPLAFT software aimed at Peruvian gaming in three Spanish searches (gaming-specific, consultancy/outsourced compliance officer, general PLAFT software for Peru). State tools: SUCTR (online monitoring of all ~72.5k machines for MINCETUR/SUNAT, not AML), ROSEL and the PLAFT portal (filing channels only), and SBS list-check pages. Law firms such as PRCP publish SPLAFT guides, which suggests a consulting market exists. Not checked: international and LatAm AML/KYC SaaS, casino-management or player-tracking systems that may include AML modules, and in-house systems at large chains.
result.duty: Ley 27693 makes casinos and slot-machine operators reporting entities. Res. SBS 01015-2026 (dated 6 Apr 2026, published in El Peruano 8 Apr 2026) updates Res. SBS 1695-2016 and also amends the sanctions regulation (Res. SBS 5389-2013). It covers legal entities that run casinos and/or slot machines, and for the first time remote games, remote sports betting and betting rooms. Duties: a risk-based SPLAFT with 13 minimum components; a compliance officer accredited to the UIF (exclusive or part-time, plus an alternate; designation reported within 15 business days); due diligence on clients, workers and suppliers; checks against UN lists and asset freezes; annual staff training; internal and external audit; operations register; suspicious-transaction reports (ROS) filed via ROSEL; an annual compliance-officer report (IAOC) sent to MINCETUR and the UIF. Anonymous betting is eliminated. A new alert-reporting guide via ROSEL (Res. SBS 01219-2026, 24 Apr 2026) also applies to reporting entities. MINCETUR supervises and sanctions. A search summary attributed to press coverage put fines at up to about 8 UIT for the gravest failures; I did not confirm this, and a 2023 PRCP infographic on the general regime gave 7-100 UIT for very serious breaches. Not verified: effective date, adaptation window, and whether there are casino-specific register thresholds (the general rule is USD 10k per operation and USD 50k per month for multiple operations).
result.market: MINCETUR's vice-minister (El Peruano, July 2026) cited 19 authorised casinos and 714 registered slot rooms with about 72,500 machines. The number of distinct legal entities is lower because chains own many rooms; the exact count was not found. Remote betting and gaming platforms are newly in scope (MINCETUR has authorised and blocks many; count not verified). Penalty pressure is real: in Jan-Aug 2022 MINCETUR made 1,346 inspections and sanctioned 10 firms for not filing the annual compliance-officer report.
result.reason: The duty is real. Res. SBS 01015-2026 (dated 6 Apr, published 8 Apr 2026) updates Res. SBS 1695-2016 under Ley 27693. It requires a risk-based SPLAFT with 13 minimum components (compliance officer, due diligence, annual training, audit, operations register, STRs, annual compliance-officer report) and now covers remote and sports betting. MINCETUR supervises and fines; it fined 10 firms in 2022 for missing the annual report. About 714 registered slot rooms plus 19 casinos (July 2026). Searches found no Peru-specific gaming SPLAFT software, but law firms and consultants serve the sector. LatAm AML tools and casino-management systems were not checked. Many rooms belong to chains, the compliance officer can be part-time, and the adaptation deadline is unverified. The niche is real but small.

result.competitor: I found no private software. Free state tools cover the current steps: the MINEM Ventanilla Única de Formalización Minera, the IGAFOM virtual system, and free MINEM IGAFOM technical-assistance campaigns run with miners' associations (e.g. AMAPATAZ in La Libertad). Private environmental consultancies and engineers prepare IGAFOMs, since the preventive part must be signed by a licensed engineer or environmental professional. I found no consultancy names or prices.
result.duty: REINFO-registered miners must complete Formalización Minera Integral (IGAFOM, mining title or exploitation contract, technical file, AOM) through the Ventanilla Única. REINFO is in force until 31 Dec 2026 or until the MAPE law takes effect (Ley 32537 amending DL 1293, per Gestión, ProActivo and Expreso coverage). The MAPE bill had not been sent to Congress (expected mid-October 2026). The Executive rules out another extension and proposes a simplified process for miners with valid status, with details left to later regulations. The penalty is losing REINFO cover, so mining activity becomes illegal. The successor rules are unknown, so the transition duty cannot be verified.
result.market: About 31,000 miners are registered in REINFO (the minister cited 31,000; the claim says 23,861 have valid status). An Energiminas analysis gives 82,130 registrations in total, of which about 23,061 were valid and 2,049 had completed formalization. Regional example: 2,704 registered in Ica.
result.reason: REINFO really does end on 31 Dec 2026, or earlier if the MAPE law takes effect first (Ley 32537). The "transition" duty, though, is not defined yet. As of early October 2026 the Executive had not sent the MAPE bill to Congress; it was due mid-October. Minister Shinno says there will be no new extension and that miners with valid REINFO status will get a "much more simplified" formalization process, with details left to later regulations and supreme decrees. So there are no requirements yet for a kit to cover. Congress has extended REINFO again and again, so another extension is possible. The current work (IGAFOM, Ventanilla Única) has free MINEM help. I found no private software. Buyers are informal, hard to reach and unlikely to pay. The product could be obsolete within months.

result.competitor: I found no association-side software. The tools that exist all belong to municipalities: Magdalena's 'Motocuy' app, Chorrillos' 'Moto Segura' QR system, a shared QR database planned by Piura, Castilla and Veintiséis de Octubre, and student projects for Tambopata and Puente Piedra. These are the state's own systems, which are out of scope, but they may cover part of the padrón job. Associations keep padrones by hand through municipal resolutions; the Huamachuco-style files show a cap of 300 units with 268 operating. Generic tools that track fleet document expiry were not checked separately.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force under Peruvian law. Ley 31917 and its regulation, DS 011-2025-MTC (published 27 Jul 2025), say the service may only be provided by a legal entity that holds a Permiso de Operación from the district municipality. Each vehicle also needs a Certificado de Operación, and drivers need credentials. The MTC procedure sheets (trámites 2364/2365) give the permit 10 years, renewable, with the request filed within 60 calendar days before expiry. One Piura report says 6 years, so the term is still disputed. Other dates: vests and holographic stickers from 22 Jan 2026; medical and psychological tests required until 31 Dec 2026; the mental-health test is suspended until Dec 2027; and the MTC had to add a national register of transport operators to SINARETT. DS 004-2026-MTC (20 Jan 2026) sets implementation measures, but I could not read its text (the Congreso PDF returned 404). One outlet says the regulation takes effect 22 Aug 2026, which conflicts with the other dates. Sanctions for legal entities were not read. I found no confirmation of a 2026 extension or of the amending bill passing.
result.market: There is no official count of authorised legal entities; the SINARETT operator register has published no total. A 2019 bill estimated more than 600,000 mototaxis in Peru, about half of them in Lima. One district, San Juan de Miraflores, estimates about 6,000 formal units. Associations typically hold 100 to 300 units each, which suggests a few thousand associations nationwide. That number is an inference, not verified.
result.reason: The duty is real and new, and I found no association-side tool. But the permit itself renews only every 10 years (or 6), so the recurring work is mostly upkeep of the driver and vehicle padrón: SOAT or CAT, CITV and licence expiries, adding and removing units. Buyers are informal, low-margin mototaxi associations that already resist enforcement (Piura protest marches), so willingness to pay is doubtful. Municipalities are building their own QR and padrón systems, which could cover the same data. Enforcement is weak because municipalities lack money and staff, and deadlines are slipping into 2027. The MVP would be simple and associations could be reached through federations, but the money looks thin.

result.competitor: I found no compliance-specific product for authorization files, the art. 14 information pack or sanctions tracking. SieWeb, an integrated management system for nurseries and schools since 2000, handles enrolment, grades, bank collections and data transfer to MINEDU, but not the compliance packet. SIAGIE is the free mandatory MINEDU system for enrolment and grades. Identicole is a MINEDU lookup site for parents, not a compliance tool. I found no information on Cubicol or Colegium. result.duty: Ley 32562 (published 22 Mar 2026) amends Ley 26549 and is in force. It repeals DS 005-2021-MINEDU. Art. 2-4: a school needs operating authorization from the DRE/UGEL before promoting enrolment, and the DRE has 90 business days to decide. Art. 14.1: each year, at least 30 calendar days before enrolment, the school must give parents truthful written information covering internal rules, enrolment and pension fees, entry fee, a 5-year fee history, admission requirements and vacancies, curriculum, calendar and maximum class size. Art. 14.2: fee information again at least 30 days before the school year ends. Sanctions: operating without authorization costs 50-100 UIT. Minor infractions cost 0.5-2 UIT, serious ones 2-20 UIT, and very serious ones 20-80 UIT plus suspension or closure. The owner or promoter is jointly liable (art. 3.4). The law sets no adaptation period for existing schools. The 60-day regulation deadline was missed: only a draft regulation was published (RM 307-2026-MINEDU, 22/23 May 2026), and I found no final DS as of Oct 2026. Indecopi separately supervises information duties and can fine up to 450 UIT.
result.market: The 2023 Censo Educativo (MINEDU, via Gestion, 16 Feb 2024) counted 13,664 private school sites, out of 68,957 in total. That counts sites, not institutions. More than 3.5M students attend private education (IPAE, 2023 data). I did not get the 2025 private total or the counts for CETPRO, academias and PRONOEI.
result.reason: The duty is real. Ley 32562 (El Peruano, 22 Mar 2026) amends Ley 26549 and requires prior authorization before enrolment promotion. Art. 14 requires written information to parents (internal rules, fees, a 5-year fee history, vacancies and more) 30 days before enrolment, and fee information 30 days before the school year ends. Fines run from 0.5 to 100 UIT, with closure possible, and owners are jointly liable. The regulation is only a draft (RM 307-2026-MINEDU); I found no final DS. I found no compliance-specific product, but SieWeb-type school systems are adjacent. The work is mostly annual or one-off document assembly, which lawyers and consultants already do. Willingness to pay among small informal schools looks low, so the market is limited, even with about 13.7k private school sites (2023 census).

Duties are real. APCI requires an annual Informe Anual and Plan Anual through SIGCTI. The 2025 deadline was extended to 30 Jun 2026 (RDE 058-2026/APCI-DE). Not filing blocks the IGV refund. SUNAT beneficial-owner filing (DL 1372, DS 003-2019-EF, FV 3800, RS 168-2025/SUNAT) carries a fine of 5-50 UIT. Whether a small association with little income must file, and how often, is unclear. Duty is real but is a product-sale restriction, not a recurring filing. Andina (SENASA, 2024) confirms: only registered pesticides, no expired or prohibited stock, Ia/Ib sales need an agronomist prescription, and unannounced inspections. I found no periodic report, sales book, e-prescription, fine schedule or shop count. The duty is real. RS 000143-2026-SUSALUD/SUP, published 26 Aug 2026, requires private IPRESS on SITEDS Cliente to migrate to the Acredita Salud Platform or adapt their own systems by 31 Oct 2026. The resolution reports 386 of 508 migrated, which leaves about 122. The opportunity is weak. It is a one-off migration with only 3 weeks left. The duty is real. LVGLP must register prices in Osinergmin's PRICE system and post them in the shop. The duty chain is real but indirect. Ley 29419 sets up municipal registration of recicladores. The MEF incentive sheet requires sales documents from registered associations, or liquidaciones de compra to registered recicladores, to count toward RSIV. That is a municipal incentive condition. It is not a mandatory recurring filing by the associations. I found no recycler-association software in 3 searches, but that is not proof none exists. I found no 2026 methodology; the only one is the 2025 sheet. Peru has about 59 formal associations in Lima and Callao (opinion column), against 180k recyclers by one estimate. Buyers are poor and few, and the real buyer is the municipality, which is the state's system. Low willingness to pay, so the score stays at 3.

The duty is real. Markets need a corporate licencia de funcionamiento under TUO Ley 28976 (DS 163-2020-PCM). The ITSE certificate is valid 2 years. The licence itself has indefinite validity. Stalls get ITSE ex post. No dedicated tracker for market juntas turned up in two searches. Free PRODUCE guidance (RM 155-2021) is only referential. The market is about 2,612 markets and 328,946 fixed stalls (INEI CENAMA 2016, now dated). The duty is real. DS 002-2018-PCM sets a 2-year ITSE validity, and renewal needs a fee plus a sworn declaration (Anexo 5).
